plan_a_advantages: More trail-specific workouts (hill repeats, long runs) that mimic race conditions.
Includes a dedicated 'tempo' session for building speed and lactate threshold.
Greater overall volume of training, contributing to a stronger aerobic base.
plan_b_advantages: Lower overall training volume, potentially reducing the risk of overtraining.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates more targeted trail-specific workouts like hill repeats and longer runs at moderate intensity. These sessions directly address the demands of trail running – navigating varied terrain and building the muscular endurance needed for sustained effort. Plan B, while including interval training, relies heavily on aerobic runs and cross-training, which, while beneficial for base fitness, don't adequately prepare the athlete for the specific challenges of a trail race. Plan A’s focus on simulating race conditions through hill work and longer runs will translate more effectively to improved race performance.
